Validate the Structural Integrity of a Derivation Graph

Source: R/trace_validate.R
validate_trace_graph.Rd

Runs structural integrity checks over the derivation graph behind trace_chains() and trace_impact() and returns a tidy diagnostic report. These are purely structural graph checks, not traceability scoring: they say whether the graph itself is well formed before any coverage or level is read off it.

Usage

validate_trace_graph(trace_model, adam_derivations = NULL)

Arguments

trace_model

A trace_model from build_trace_model().

adam_derivations

Optional data.frame of ADaM-to-ADaM derivations with columns from_dataset, from_var, to_dataset, to_var, as in trace_chains().

Value

A tibble with one row per node per failing check: check (one of "cycle", "dangling_edge", "orphan", "disconnected"), dataset, variable, role, and a readable detail. Zero rows means the graph is structurally clean.

Details

The graph is the same one the rest of the engine uses: nodes are ADaM and SDTM variables and a directed edge runs from a derived variable to its source (A -> B reads "A is derived from B"). ADaM-to-SDTM edges come from the trace model's mapping; ADaM-to-ADaM edges are added when supplied through adam_derivations, exactly as in trace_chains(). Four checks are reported, one row per node per failing check:

  • cycle: the node is part of a circular derivation chain (a variable that derives, directly or transitively, from itself). Found with a standard strongly-connected-component search, so every node in the cycle is flagged.

  • dangling_edge: a derivation edge (always from adam_derivations) names this node as a source or dependent, but it is not present as a node in the trace model. The edge points at something that does not exist.

  • orphan: the variable takes part in no derivation edge at all (an isolated node) - an ADaM variable mapped to nothing, or an SDTM variable read by nothing.

  • disconnected: the node belongs to a connected component (two or more nodes joined by derivations) that contains no SDTM variable, so no path in that component can ever reach a source.

A node can appear in more than one check. Cycle detection, reachability, and connected components are standard graph algorithms; nothing here invents a domain weight, threshold, or score.

See also

trace_lineage() for ancestry and dependent queries, trace_problems() for ADaM-side traceability issues, trace_chains() for the graph model itself.

Examples

adam <- data.frame(
  dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE"), variable = c("AGE", "AAGE"),
  label = c("Age", "Analysis Age")
)
sdtm <- data.frame(dataset = "DM", variable = "AGE", label = "Age")
map <- data.frame(
  adam_dataset = "ADSL", adam_var = "AGE",
  sdtm_domain = "DM", sdtm_var = "AGE", confidence = 1
)
tm <- build_trace_model(adam, sdtm, mapping = map)

# A clean mapping reports nothing except the orphan ADAE.AAGE.
validate_trace_graph(tm)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   check  dataset variable role  detail                                         
#>   <chr>  <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>                                          
#> 1 orphan ADAE    AAGE     adam  isolated node: takes part in no derivation edge

# A circular derivation is detected.
cyc <- data.frame(
  from_dataset = c("ADSL", "ADAE"), from_var = c("AGE", "AAGE"),
  to_dataset   = c("ADAE", "ADSL"), to_var   = c("AAGE", "AGE")
)
validate_trace_graph(tm, adam_derivations = cyc)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   check dataset variable role  detail                                           
#>   <chr> <chr>   <chr>    <chr> <chr>                                            
#> 1 cycle ADAE    AAGE     adam  part of a circular derivation chain among: ADAE.…
#> 2 cycle ADSL    AGE      adam  part of a circular derivation chain among: ADAE.…
